info.title: Factrove HTTP API
info.description: Generated from `@factrove/contracts` schemas and the HTTP operation catalog. Product routes live under `/api/v1`. Auth and API key management live under `/api/auth`. Do not treat this file as hand-written. Run `pnpm docs:openapi` after contract or route-catalog changes.

tags.name: Artifacts
tags.description: Upload, list, rename, delete, detail, and content.

tags.name: Public
tags.description: Anonymous share detail, unlock, and HTML.

get.summary: Check that the API is initialized
get.description: Returns `{ status: "ok" }` after the process has started. No credentials.

200.description: The API is initialized.

get.summary: Return the caller and current organization
get.description: Reads the session cookie or `Authorization: Bearer` API key. A session uses `activeOrganizationId` when the caller is a member of that organization. Otherwise the organization is the caller's only membership, or null when they have none or more than one. An API key has no active organization and uses the sole-membership rule. A present Authorization header that is not a valid key does not fall back to the session cookie. `x-api-key` does not authenticate.

200.description: The signed-in user and current organization.

post.summary: Create an account with email and password
post.description: Better Auth email/password sign-up. Email verification is off. Passwords are 8 to 128 characters, the same limits createAuth passes to Better Auth. This route is rate limited to 10 requests per 60 seconds per client address. The response body is Better Auth JSON, not the product `{ error: { code, message } }` envelope. A successful sign-up sets the session cookie and can return the user. It also sends one invite email to that address. A plus-address such as name+tag@example.com is valid and is stored in lower case with the plus tag kept. EMAIL_TRANSPORT selects the sender. log writes the message and does not send it. smtp uses the configured SMTP server. brevo sends POST https://api.brevo.com/v3/smtp/email. An unset transport is log. Sending failure does not roll back the account. A duplicate email does not send another message.

requestBody.description: Display name, email, and password (8 to 128 characters).

200.description: Account created. Better Auth JSON that includes the user.

400.description: Better Auth validation failure, such as `PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT`, `PASSWORD_TOO_LONG`, or `INVALID_EMAIL`.

422.description: The email is already registered. Better Auth `USER_ALREADY_EXISTS_USE_ANOTHER_EMAIL`.

429.description: Too many sign-up attempts from this client address.

post.summary: Sign in with email and password
post.description: Better Auth email/password sign-in. Passwords are 8 to 128 characters. Rate limited to 10 requests per 60 seconds per client address. Sets the session cookie. The response body is Better Auth JSON.

200.description: Signed in. Better Auth JSON and a session cookie.

400.description: Better Auth validation failure, such as `INVALID_EMAIL` or `PASSWORD_TOO_LONG`.

401.description: Unknown user or wrong password. Better Auth `INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD`.

429.description: Too many sign-in attempts from this client address.

post.description: Requires a browser session. Do not send `Authorization`. A request that also sends it is 401 with message `API key management requires a browser session.` Cookie writes need `Origin` or `Referer` to be `WEB_ORIGIN` or `PUBLIC_BASE_URL`. A missing or different origin is 403 `FORBIDDEN` before Better Auth runs. The secret is returned once in `key`. The plugin stores only a hash. Keys use the `ftrv_` prefix and do not expire. The plugin's own per-key rate limit is off.

requestBody.description: A name is required, 1 to 32 characters.

x-codeSamples.label: Sign in and create a key
x-codeSamples.source:
api=http://localhost:3001
origin=http://localhost:3000
jar=$(mktemp)

curl -sS -c "$jar" -X POST "$api/api/auth/sign-up/email" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Origin: $origin" \
  -d '{"name":"Local Owner","email":"owner@example.com","password":"replace-this-password"}'

curl -sS -b "$jar" -X POST "$api/api/auth/api-key/create" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Origin: $origin" \
  -d '{"name":"cli"}'

200.description: The new key, including `key` once.

400.description: Empty or missing name is Better Auth `NAME_REQUIRED` (`API Key name is required.`). A name longer than 32 characters is `INVALID_NAME_LENGTH`.

401.description: No browser session, or Authorization was also sent.

403.description: Cookie write whose Origin or Referer is not WEB_ORIGIN or PUBLIC_BASE_URL. Code `FORBIDDEN`.

error.message: This request origin is not allowed.

get.summary: List API keys for the session
get.description: Requires a browser session. Returns names and starting characters, not the secret. Better Auth JSON `{ apiKeys, total }`.

200.description: Keys for the signed-in user, without `key`.

401.description: No browser session, or Authorization was also sent.

post.description: Requires a browser session. Do not send `Authorization`. Cookie writes need `Origin` or `Referer` to be `WEB_ORIGIN` or `PUBLIC_BASE_URL`. A missing or different origin is 403 `FORBIDDEN`. Another user's key id is 404. After delete, that key fails closed on product routes.

200.description: The key was deleted.

401.description: No browser session, or Authorization was also sent.

403.description: Cookie write whose Origin or Referer is not WEB_ORIGIN or PUBLIC_BASE_URL. Code `FORBIDDEN`.

error.message: This request origin is not allowed.

404.description: The key id is unknown to this session.

post.description: Accepts one non-empty `.html` or `.htm` file as multipart field `file`, optional `accessType` (`private` default, or `org_shared`), and optional `name`. `name` is one line of 1 to 120 characters. When `name` is omitted, the stored name is the file name without `.html` or `.htm` when that stem is one line of 1 to 120 characters. An empty stem, a stem longer than 120 characters, or a stem that is not one line stores null, and the upload still succeeds. An invalid submitted `name` is `400 INVALID_REQUEST` and stores no row. The backend assigns `text/html`. Maximum size is 10 MiB. Each request creates a new artifact. The object is written first, then the row. A storage failure leaves no row. Cookie-authenticated writes also require Origin or Referer to be WEB_ORIGIN or PUBLIC_BASE_URL.

requestBody.description: One file, an optional access type, and an optional library name.

x-codeSamples.label: Upload hello.html
Upload hello.html
x-codeSamples.source:
import os
import requests

with open("./fixtures/hello.html", "rb") as handle:
    response = requests.post(
        "http://localhost:3001/api/v1/artifacts",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['FACTROVE_API_KEY']}"},
        files={"file": ("hello.html", handle, "text/html")},
    )

400.description: Invalid multipart body, access type, name, or UTF-8. An invalid name is NFC-normalized, then rejected when it contains U+0000–U+001F, U+007F–U+009F, U+2028, or U+2029 before trimming, or when the trimmed value is not 1 to 120 Unicode code points. That response is `400 INVALID_REQUEST` with message `name must be one line of 1 to 120 characters.` Other failures use `INVALID_REQUEST` or `ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED`.

error.message: The file is not valid UTF-8.
Organization sharing requires membership in an organization.

403.description: Cookie write from a disallowed origin. Code `FORBIDDEN`.

error.message: This request origin is not allowed.

413.description: The file is larger than 10 MiB. Code `FILE_TOO_LARGE`.

error.message: The file exceeds the 10 MiB limit.

415.description: The file is not HTML. Code `UNSUPPORTED_FILE_TYPE`.

503.description: Object storage failed. Code `STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE`. No artifact row is stored.

get.description: `view=mine` (default) is artifacts the caller created. `view=org` is org_shared artifacts in the caller's current organization, including other creators. With no current organization, `view=org` is an empty list. Sorted by createdAt descending, then id descending. The whole list is returned.

200.description: Matching artifacts.

error.message: view must be mine or org.

put.description: Owner only. Multipart field `file` is the same HTML validation as create: one non-empty `.html` or `.htm` file, at most 10 MiB, UTF-8. Optional `name` is set in the same conditional update as the new object and the revision check. Omit `name` and that update does not change the column, so the current name stays. An invalid `name` is `400 INVALID_REQUEST` and leaves the current HTML in place. `accessType` is rejected. The id, current access, and any share token stay the same. The new object is written first, then the row points at it. Another replace of the same revision is `409 CONTENT_CONFLICT` and does not change the name. An acknowledged or successfully reconciled update returns 200 even if a later replace has landed since. The 200 shows the artifact's current state, which may already include a later replace. A content commit that throws can still land later, and that landing sets the name when this request included one. If the client sees 500 it should GET the artifact before retrying. Cookie-authenticated writes need an allowed Origin.

requestBody.description: One HTML file and an optional library name. Do not send accessType.

200.description: The same artifact id with the new size and upload time. The 200 shows the artifact's current state, which may already include a later replace.

400.description: Invalid multipart body, accessType on replace, name, or UTF-8. An invalid name uses the same NFC, trim, and control-character rule as upload and is code `INVALID_REQUEST` with message `name must be one line of 1 to 120 characters.`

error.message: accessType cannot be changed when replacing content.

403.description: Cookie write from a disallowed origin. Code `FORBIDDEN`.

error.message: This request origin is not allowed.

404.description: Unknown artifact, or the caller is not the owner. Code `ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND`.

error.message: Another replace finished first. Upload again to replace the current content.

413.description: The file is larger than 10 MiB. Code `FILE_TOO_LARGE`.

error.message: The file exceeds the 10 MiB limit.

415.description: The file is not HTML. Code `UNSUPPORTED_FILE_TYPE`.

500.description: The replace commit threw after the object was written. The new bytes, and the name when this request sent one, may already be live. GET the artifact before retrying. Code `INTERNAL_ERROR`.

503.description: Object storage failed before the row was updated. Code `STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE`.

get.summary: Download artifact HTML or converted Markdown
get.description: Default format is HTML, the stored bytes, `Content-Type: text/html`. `format=markdown` converts that HTML on a worker and returns `text/markdown`. Markdown is not stored. `Accept` does not choose the format. Optional `access` is a short-lived HMAC grant for HTML in the viewer iframe and authenticates the request by itself when no Authorization or x-api-key header is present. A present credential header disables the grant. Markdown ignores it. Missing credentials without a valid grant are the same 404 as an unknown id.

parameters.name: access
parameters.description: Viewer content grant. HTML only, at most five minutes, ignored when a credential header is present. A valid grant returns 200 with no cookie or bearer key.

200.description: HTML (`text/html`) or Markdown (`text/markdown`) bytes with charset=utf-8.

error.message: format must be html or markdown.

404.description: Unknown or unreadable artifact, including missing credentials without a valid `access` grant. Code `ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND`.

413.description: Stored HTML exceeds the Markdown input limit. Code `CONTENT_TOO_LARGE`.

error.message: HTML exceeds the Markdown conversion limit.
HTML took too long to convert to Markdown.

503.description: Object storage failed (`STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE`) or the Markdown conversion pool is full (`CONVERSION_UNAVAILABLE`). Neither sets Retry-After.

error.message: Markdown conversion is busy. Try again.

patch.summary: Share a private artifact with the confirmed organization
patch.description: Owner only. JSON body `{ "accessType": "org_shared", "organizationId": "<current organization id>" }` switches a private artifact to `org_shared` and sets `organizationId` to that id. The id must be the caller's current membership. The only explicit row lock is the artifact. The organization foreign-key check takes an implicit KEY SHARE lock on the organization row. The update does not lock the user, the session, or membership rows. It re-checks membership and, for a session, that the session is still present and unexpired, in the conditional UPDATE. That statement is the linearization point. A different current organization at that snapshot is `409 ORGANIZATION_CHANGED` and does not write. A membership removal, organization deletion, active-organization change, or session revocation that commits before the statement reads its rows returns 409, 400, or `401 UNAUTHENTICATED` with no write. An authorization change that commits after that snapshot can land before the transaction commits and does not cancel the share. A deadlock, serialization failure, or lock timeout retries once and then returns `409 ORGANIZATION_CHANGED` with no write. About 16 seconds is the budget for those two attempts, not a deadline for this endpoint. The update matches the id, the creator, and `accessType` private, so concurrent requests leave one organization-shared row. An artifact that is already `org_shared` returns 200 and does not change its organization, share token, or share password, for any confirmed organizationId and whether or not the caller has a current organization. This route does not create or remove a public share, and it does not change an organization-shared artifact back to private. Cookie-authenticated writes need Origin or Referer to be WEB_ORIGIN or PUBLIC_BASE_URL.

requestBody.description: Share the artifact with the organization the caller confirmed. That id must be the current membership.

200.description: The artifact is org_shared. A repeat request for an artifact that is already org_shared returns it without writing, for any confirmed organizationId.

400.description: This route shares a private artifact with the confirmed organization. A JSON array, and a JSON object with any other shape, including accessType private or a missing organizationId, is `400 INVALID_REQUEST` with message `Send { "accessType": "org_shared", "organizationId": "<current organization id>" }. This shares a private artifact with that organization.` Malformed JSON, null, and JSON primitives are `400 INVALID_REQUEST` with message `The request is invalid.` A body whose media type is not application/json is `400 INVALID_REQUEST` with message `Send JSON with Content-Type application/json.` A private artifact and no current organization is `400 ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED` and the row stays private. An id that is not a UUID is also `400 INVALID_REQUEST`.

error.message: Artifact id must be a UUID.

401.description: Missing credentials, or a session that was revoked or expired before the conditional update read it. Code `UNAUTHENTICATED`. The artifact is not written. A revocation that commits after that snapshot does not cancel a share the statement already accepted.

403.description: Cookie write from a disallowed origin. Code `FORBIDDEN`.

error.message: This request origin is not allowed.

404.description: Unknown artifact, or the caller is not the owner. Code `ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND`.

409.description: The artifact is still private and organizationId is not the caller's current membership when the conditional update reads, or a deadlock, serialization failure, or lock timeout persisted after one retry. Code `ORGANIZATION_CHANGED`. The artifact is not written. An authorization change that commits after that snapshot does not produce this response and does not undo the share. About 16 seconds is the budget for the two attempts, not an endpoint deadline.

error.message: The current organization changed. Confirm the organization and try again.

413.description: The JSON body is larger than 102,400 bytes. Code `FILE_TOO_LARGE` with message `The request is too large.`

500.description: JSON error envelope `{ error: { code, message } }`.

delete.description: Owner only. Deletes the artifact row and the current HTML object. The creator is the only caller who can delete. Organization role is not consulted, so an organization admin who did not create the artifact cannot delete it. A missing id and a caller who is not the creator, including a member who can read an org_shared artifact, return the same 404 as an unknown id. The object for the revision that was read is removed first. The row is deleted only while that creator, revision, and object key are still current. A replace that commits in between keeps its row, and this request reads that row and tries again. A missing object still allows that row delete. A storage failure keeps the row. The object may already be gone, so retry DELETE. A public link stops working because the row, including its share token, is gone. Older objects left behind by a failed content replace are not swept. Cookie-authenticated writes need an allowed Origin.

204.description: The artifact row and its current HTML object are gone. The response has no body.

403.description: Cookie write from a disallowed origin. Code `FORBIDDEN`.

error.message: This request origin is not allowed.

404.description: Unknown artifact, or the caller is not the owner. An organization admin or another member who can read the artifact gets this same body. Code `ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND`.

500.description: The row delete failed after the current object was removed. Retry the delete. A missing object is treated as already removed. Code `INTERNAL_ERROR`.

503.description: Object storage failed before the row was deleted. Code `STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE`. The row is kept. The object may already be gone, so retry DELETE.

get.description: Owner and, for org_shared artifacts, organization members can read this. Missing credentials, an invalid key, and anyone who cannot read the artifact get the same 404 as an unknown id. This route does not return 401. A session-authenticated response may append `?access=` on `contentUrl` so the sandboxed iframe can load HTML without cookies. API-key responses omit that grant.

200.description: Artifact metadata, including whether a public share is active.

400.description: The id is not a UUID. Code `INVALID_REQUEST`.

error.message: Artifact id must be a UUID.

404.description: Unknown or unreadable artifact, including missing or invalid credentials. Code `ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND`.

patch.description: Owner only. Changes the library name and leaves the HTML object, content revision, access, organization, and share columns unchanged. The creator is the only caller who can rename. Organization role is not consulted, so an organization admin who did not create the artifact cannot rename it. A missing id and a caller who is not the creator, including a member who can read an org_shared artifact, return the same 404 as an unknown id. Cookie-authenticated writes need an allowed Origin.

requestBody.description: The new library name. This route does not change access or content, and it cannot clear a name.

200.description: The same artifact with the new name.

400.description: The rename body must be { "name": "<library name>" } and nothing else. An invalid name is NFC-normalized, then rejected when it contains U+0000–U+001F, U+007F–U+009F, U+2028, or U+2029 before trimming, or when the trimmed value is not 1 to 120 Unicode code points. That response is `400 INVALID_REQUEST` with message `name must be one line of 1 to 120 characters.` A JSON array or any other object shape is `400 INVALID_REQUEST` with message `Send { "name": "<library name>" }. The name is one line of 1 to 120 characters.` Malformed JSON, null, and JSON primitives are `400 INVALID_REQUEST` with message `The request is invalid.` A body whose media type is not application/json is `400 INVALID_REQUEST` with message `Send JSON with Content-Type application/json.` A path id that fails UUID validation is also `400 INVALID_REQUEST`. A body larger than 102,400 bytes is `413 FILE_TOO_LARGE` with message `The request is too large.`

error.message: Artifact id must be a UUID.

error.message: This request origin is not allowed.

404.description: Unknown artifact, or the caller is not the owner. An organization admin or another member who can read the artifact gets this same body. Code `ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND`.

413.description: The JSON body is larger than 102,400 bytes. Code `FILE_TOO_LARGE` with message `The request is too large.`

post.description: Creates a public link, or returns the existing one while the current key can still read the token. An optional JSON body `{ password }` sets or replaces the link password. Omitting the password keeps the current one. Passwords are 10 to 128 NFC characters, at least four distinct characters, not all whitespace, and not on the bundled common-password list. Repeating the request without a password returns the same link. Cookie writes require an allowed Origin.

delete.summary: Remove the password from a shared link
delete.description: When the artifact is shared, the share URL stays the same, `passwordProtected` becomes false, and existing unlock grants become invalid. When the artifact is not shared, the response is `{ shared: false, shareUrl: null, passwordProtected: false }`.

200.description: The current share state. A shared artifact stays shared without a password. An unshared artifact stays unshared.

error.message: This request origin is not allowed.

get.description: No session. The response omits creator, organization, access type, and the share URL. An inactive, unknown, or revoked token is `404 ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND` and does not say whether the artifact exists. A password-protected share without a valid `X-Factrove-Share-Grant` is `401 PASSWORD_REQUIRED`. The view allowance is charged per visitor address before the link lookup and password check, so a 401 or 404 still consumes it. IPv6 addresses share a /64. A charge grants two companion content loads for 30 seconds. View units are limited to 60 per 60 seconds per client address, in memory on each API process. A content request without a remaining companion charges another view unit before its own lookup. That 429 does not include Retry-After. Responses send Referrer-Policy: no-referrer and X-Robots-Tag: noindex.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Public share token from the owner share URL. The stored column is a hash, not this value.

parameters.name: x-factrove-share-grant
parameters.description: Unlock grant from POST /unlock. Never a cookie and never part of a URL. The HTTP header is `X-Factrove-Share-Grant`.

200.description: Public artifact metadata. `contentUrl` may include a short-lived `ticket` query after a grant.

401.description: The link needs a password and the grant is missing or invalid. Code `PASSWORD_REQUIRED`.

404.description: The link is not active. Code `ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND`.

429.description: The visitor view allowance is already spent, including when the response would have been 401 or 404. Code `RATE_LIMITED`. No Retry-After. Charged per address before lookup. IPv6 addresses share a /64.

error.message: Too many requests. Try again later.

post.description: No session. JSON `{ password }`. A matching password returns `{ grant: { token, expiresAt } }` valid for 15 minutes. A link with no password returns `{ grant: null }`. A wrong password is `401 PASSWORD_INCORRECT`. An inactive link is `404 ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND`. A missing or non-JSON body is `400 INVALID_REQUEST` before any password throttle is charged. Client failures allow 10 per 10 minutes. Share failures allow 30 per 10 minutes, charged only after a wrong password. An exhausted share is `429 RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After` and no hash verification. A saturated Argon2 gate, or a share whose remaining slots are all in flight, is `503 UNLOCK_UNAVAILABLE` with `Retry-After`. This route ignores a leftover session cookie and does not apply the cookie origin guard.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Public share token from the owner share URL. The stored column is a hash, not this value.

200.description: A grant for a protected link, or null when the link has no password.

error.message: Send the password as a string.

404.description: The link is not active. Code `ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND`.

429.description: Too many password attempts for this client or this share. Code `RATE_LIMITED`. Every password-throttle 429 sends Retry-After. Counters are in memory on each API process.

error.message: Too many password attempts. Try again later.

503.description: Password verification is busy. Code `UNLOCK_UNAVAILABLE`. Includes Retry-After.

error.message: Password verification is busy. Try again.

get.description: No session. Markdown is not offered. A password-protected link needs a `ticket` query minted on a granted detail response. The ticket lasts 60 seconds and is honored at most 3 times per API process. Content on a protected link without a valid ticket is `401 PASSWORD_REQUIRED`. Reverse proxies should not log `?ticket=`.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Public share token from the owner share URL. The stored column is a hash, not this value.

parameters.name: ticket
parameters.description: Short-lived content ticket for a password-protected link. Not used on an open link.

200.description: HTML bytes with the same sandbox CSP as a signed-in viewer.

401.description: Protected content without a valid ticket. Code `PASSWORD_REQUIRED`.

404.description: The link is not active. Code `ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND`.

429.description: The visitor view allowance is already spent, including when the link is missing or the ticket check would fail. Code `RATE_LIMITED`. No Retry-After. Charged per address before lookup, unless a companion grant from a recent detail remains. IPv6 addresses share a /64.

error.message: Too many requests. Try again later.

503.description: Object storage failed while reading HTML. Code `STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE`. No Retry-After.

bearerAuth.description: Factrove API key, usually prefixed `ftrv_`. Send `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Product routes do not accept `x-api-key` as a credential. A present Authorization header that is not a valid key does not fall back to the session cookie.

sessionCookie.name: better-auth.session_token
sessionCookie.description: Better Auth session cookie from email/password sign-in. On an https API origin the name is `__Secure-better-auth.session_token`. On http it is `better-auth.session_token`. Host-only unless AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN is set. Use a cookie jar instead of typing the name.

accessGrant.name: access
accessGrant.description: Short-lived HMAC grant for HTML content in the viewer iframe. HTML only, at most five minutes. A present Authorization or x-api-key header disables the grant. Markdown ignores it. A valid grant returns 200 without a session cookie or bearer key.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. The API sets this when an `ApiErrorException` includes `retryAfterSeconds`: every password-throttle 429 RATE_LIMITED, and 503 UNLOCK_UNAVAILABLE. Public-view 429 and Markdown 503 CONVERSION_UNAVAILABLE do not set it.

code.description: 400/404 INVALID_REQUEST: The request is missing a required field, has the wrong shape, or failed validation. Typical causes are a missing file, an invalid access type, view, format, or artifact id, or invalid UTF-8. Unmatched non-public product routes also return 404 INVALID_REQUEST with message Not found. 400 ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED: The caller asked to share with an organization but has no current organization membership. Upload with accessType org_shared and PATCH /api/v1/artifacts/{id} for a private artifact both use this code. 409 ORGANIZATION_CHANGED: PATCH /api/v1/artifacts/{id} for a private artifact named an organizationId that is not the caller's current membership when the conditional UPDATE reads, or a deadlock, serialization failure, or lock timeout persisted after one retry. The artifact is not written. That UPDATE is the linearization point: an authorization change that commits after its snapshot can land before commit and does not cancel the share. About 16 seconds is the budget for the two attempts, not an endpoint deadline. An artifact that is already org_shared returns 200 instead. 401 UNAUTHENTICATED: The product route needs a session cookie or Authorization: Bearer API key, and neither was accepted. PATCH /api/v1/artifacts/{id} also returns this when the session was revoked or expired before the conditional update read it, and does not write. A revocation that commits after that snapshot does not cancel the share. 401 PASSWORD_REQUIRED: The public share is password protected and the request did not present a valid unlock grant or content ticket. 401 PASSWORD_INCORRECT: The password sent to the public unlock route did not match. 403 FORBIDDEN: A cookie-authenticated write used an Origin or Referer that is not WEB_ORIGIN or PUBLIC_BASE_URL. 404 ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND: The artifact id is unknown, the caller cannot read it, or the public share token is not active. Rename and delete also use this body when the caller is not the creator, including an organization admin or another member who can read an org_shared artifact. Those cases share this body. 409 CONTENT_CONFLICT: Another replace of the same artifact revision finished first. Upload again to replace the current content. 413 FILE_TOO_LARGE: The upload is larger than the 10 MiB HTML limit. A JSON body larger than 102,400 bytes uses the same code with message The request is too large. 413 CONTENT_TOO_LARGE: Stored HTML is larger than the Markdown conversion input limit. 415 UNSUPPORTED_FILE_TYPE: The upload is not a .html or .htm file. 422 CONTENT_TOO_COMPLEX: Markdown conversion exceeded its time, memory, nesting, or output limit. 429 RATE_LIMITED: Too many public views from one client address, or too many password attempts. Password-attempt 429 responses include Retry-After. Public-view 429 responses do not. 500 INTERNAL_ERROR: An unexpected persistence or service failure. 503 STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE: Object storage failed. A failed upload leaves no artifact row. A failed artifact delete keeps the row. The object may already be gone, so retry DELETE. 503 CONVERSION_UNAVAILABLE: The Markdown conversion worker pool is full. This response does not include Retry-After. 503 UNLOCK_UNAVAILABLE: Password verification is busy because the process-wide Argon2 gate is saturated or every remaining share check slot is in flight. Includes Retry-After.
